properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued October 5 at 2:03AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
properties.description:
A Marine Weather Statement has been issued for the following areas...
Coastal Waters from Port Fourchon LA to Lower Atchafalaya River LA
out 20 nm...
Coastal waters from Port Fourchon Louisiana to Lower Atchafalaya
River LA from 20 to 60 NM...
Coastal waters from Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River to
Port Fourchon Louisiana from 20 to 60 NM...
Coastal waters from the Southwest Pass of the Mississippi River to
Port Fourchon Louisiana out 20 NM...

At 203 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated a cluster of showers, capable
of producing winds to around 30 knots and weak waterspouts. This
cluster of showers is generally located along a line extending from 6
nm southwest of Louisiana Offshore Oil Port to near Ship Shoal 198.
The cluster of showers was nearly stationary.
properties.instruction:
Mariners can expect widespread gusty winds to around 30 knots and
higher waves. Boaters should seek safe harbor immediately until this
activity passes.

Brief, weak waterspouts are possible with this activity. Remain on
alert in case warnings are issued for waterspout development.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or nearest law enforcement
agency. They will relay your report to the National Weather Service
forecast office.

properties.description:
Patchy dense fog has formed across the area south of I-70. Some
areas may see visibilities falling to one- quarter mile or less.

headlights, and keep extra distance between your vehicle and other
vehicles. Fog will begin to dissipate by about 9 AM EDT this
morning.

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 5 at 2:00AM CDT until October 5 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Quitman, GA
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 3:00AM EDT until October 5 at 5:15AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Quitman County in southwestern Georgia...

* WHEN...Until 515 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 300 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Georgetown, Crossroads, Hatcher, Wire Bridge, Morris and
Bonapartes Retreat.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 515 AM EDT EARLY THIS MORNING

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 5 at 2:52AM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
Pockets of dense fog have developed across parts of eastern
Kentucky early this morning, with visibility reduced to below
one-quarter mile in some locations. These conditions may persist
until near or shortly after sunrise before the fog begins to lift
or burn off.

You should expect to encounter sharp reductions in visibility if
traveling through the remainder of the overnight. Use low-beam
headlights, allow yourself extra time to reach your destination,
and increase your separation distance from other vehicles.

NWSheadline: Locally dense fog possible this morning
